title: Serbian Cafe Offers Coffee with Alpacas
paragraphs: At a cafe in northern Serbia, the hosts have soft coats, four legs and a taste for carrots!
Six alpacas walk between the tables while visitors enjoy a drink and offer them snacks. The Alpaca Cafe is part of the Tiganjica Ethno-Village resort near Stajicevo, north of Belgrade.

Alpacas come from South America and belong to the same family as llamas and camels. However, they are smaller and are known for their gentle nature, soft wool and the quiet sounds they make to communicate.
Resort owner Zoran Ostojin got the idea for the cafe after visiting a similar place in Slovenia with his wife.
"We wanted people in our country to get to know alpacas and feel this animal and its energy," he said.

His interest in animals began long before the cafe opened. As boys, he and his brother brought injured animals home to care for them. Today, the resort includes a small zoo, and its first alpaca arrived as a gift from Belgrade Zoo eight years ago.

Visits to the cafe must be booked in advance. For around $11, guests get a drink and a small bucket of carrots, lettuce and apples to feed the animals. A board lists a few rules: don't approach the alpacas from behind, and don't feed them food you have brought yourself.
According to their carer, Simona Frangi, the alpacas move away if they think someone wants to hurt them, but come closer when someone has something to offer.

And although alpacas are generally calm and friendly, each is a little different. Frangi describes a black alpaca called Ljubica as grumpy. Snezana, meanwhile, is the group leader despite being the smallest of all!
